b.351e74824c:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>D</c>écimo séptimo Kaléndas Maii Luna nona. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ sanctárum Basilíssæ et Anastásiæ, nobílium feminárum, quæ, cum essent Apostolórum discípulæ et constántes in fídei confessióne persísterent, sub Neróne Imperatóre, lingua pedibúsque præcísis, percússæ gládio, martýrii corónam adéptæ sunt.
<h>E</h>ódem die sanctórum Mártyrum Marónis, Eutychétis et Victoríni; qui, primo cum beáta Flávia Domitílla apud ínsulam Póntiam in Christi confessióne éxsules, póstmodum, sub Príncipe Nerva, liberáti, tandem, cum plúrimos ad fidem convertíssent, in persecutióne Traiáni, a Valeriáno Iúdice váriis pœnis iussi sunt intérfici.
<h>I</h>n Pérside sanctórum Mártyrum Máximi et Olympíadis, qui, sub Décio Imperatóre, fústibus et plumbátis cæsi sunt; et ad últimum cápita eórum sunt fústibus tunsa, donec ambo emítterent spíritum.
<h>F</h>erentíni, in Hérnicis, sancti Eutýchii Mártyris.
<h>M</h>yræ, in Lýcia, sancti Crescéntis, qui per ignem martýrium consummávit.
<h>I</h>n Thrácia sanctórum Mártyrum Theodóri et Pausilíppi, qui sub Hadriáno Imperatóre passi sunt.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.fb1c134010:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 15th 2027, the 9th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

<h>A</h>t Rome, the noble ladies Basilissa and Anastasia, disciples of the Apostles. Forasmuch as they stood firm in the faith under the Emperor Nero, their tongues and feet were cut off, and they gained the crown of martyrdom by being slain with the sword.
<h>U</h>pon the same day, the holy martyrs Maro, Eutyches, and Victorinus. They were first exiled to the island of Ponza, along with the blessed Flavia Domitilla, for confessing Christ, but were afterwards liberated in the reign of the Emperor Nerva. They converted many to the faith, and were at length put to death with diverse torments by order of the Judge Valerian, in the persecution under the Emperor Trajan.
<h>I</h>n Persia, under the Emperor Decius, the holy martyrs Maximus and Olympias. They were first hided with cudgels and scourges loaded with lead, and at length their heads were beaten with the cudgels until they gave up the ghost.
<h>A</h>t Fiorentino, in Campania, the holy martyr Eutychius, [at the end of the first century, possibly with some companions.]
<h>A</h>t Myra, in Lycia, holy Crescens, who achieved martyrdom by fire.
<h>I</h>n Thrace, the holy martyrs Theodore, [a Priest,] and Pausilippus, who suffered under the Emperor Hadrian, [at Heracleia, on the Sea of Marmora.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.9c311374c3:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui in Fílii tui humilitáte iacéntem mundum erexísti: fidélibus tuis perpétuam concéde lætítiam; ut, quos perpétuæ mortis eripuísti cásibus, gáudiis fácias pérfrui sempitérnis.
<h>P</h>er eúndem Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum Fílium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.467f7da150:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.
<h>T</h>hrough the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio Ss. Tiburtii, Valeriani, et Maximi Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Lux perpétua lucébit Sanctis tuis, Dómine, et ætérnitas témporum, allelúia.

<r>℣.</r> Sancti et iusti in Dómino gaudéte, allelúia.
<r>℟.</r> Vos elégit Deus in hereditátem sibi, allelúia.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>ræsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum Tibúrtii, Valeriáni et Máximi sollémnia cólimus; eórum étiam virtútes imitémur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.9947245937:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.
<h>T</h>hrough the same Jesus Christ, thy Son, Our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of Sts. Tiburtius, Valerian et Maximus, Martyrs</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Eternal light will shine over your saints, O Lord, and the eternity of times, alleluia.

<r>℣.</r> Saints and just, rejoice in the Lord, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> The Lord has chosen you for his inheritance, alleluia.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>A</c>lmighty God, for Whom holy Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus uplifted their testimony, grant, we beseech Thee, unto all whosoever call the same to solemn memory, grace to imitate the example of their godly courage.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
